Every recipe is a real problem with the code that solves it and the trap that catches people.

Parse key=value pairs without allocating

The keys borrow from input, so the whole map costs one allocation (the map itself). split_once is O(n) once, unlike split('=').collect::<Vec<_>>().

Trap: split('=') silently loses everything after a second =. A password containing = breaks the naive version.

Split a line into typed values

? on Option inside a function returning Option is the whole error strategy for parsers like this.

Count characters, not bytes

Trap: even chars() is not "user-perceived characters". "👍🏽" is two chars (emoji + skin tone). If you need grapheme clusters, use the unicode-segmentation crate.

Truncate a string safely

Case-insensitive comparison without allocating

For real international case folding use unicase — simple lowercase is not the same operation.

Replace many patterns in one pass

Cow is the right return type for "usually unchanged" transformations. serde, regex and url all use it for exactly this.

Join with a separator without the trailing comma

Format a table that lines up

Width specifiers ({:<10}, {:>8}, {:^6}) are the whole table library. For Unicode text, pad by grapheme count, not {:10} — the width specifier counts chars, and wide CJK characters count as one.

Read a whole file as lines without a trailing empty line

The one-line check people forget

Escape a string for a shell command

Trap: format!("git commit -m '{}'", msg) breaks on any message containing an apostrophe, and is a command-injection hole. Command with separate args is the only correct form.
